Caterpillar distributes its machines principally through a worldwide organization of dealers, serving 190 countries with 41 located in the United States and 109 located outside the United States [1]. For Caterpillar-branded products, the relationship with each independent dealer is memorialized in standard sales and service agreements that grant the dealer the right to purchase, sell, and service products within a specified geographic territory [2]. In exchange, the dealer is obligated to develop and promote the sale of the company's products, employ adequate sales and support personnel, perform product improvement programs, and maintain detailed books and records [3]. While the large majority of worldwide dealers are independently owned and operated, Caterpillar owns and operates a dealership in Japan named the Nippon Caterpillar Division [2]. Although dealers do not deal exclusively in Caterpillar products, sales and servicing of these products are their principal business in most cases [2]. Additionally, reciprocating engines are sold principally through the dealer network and to other manufacturers for use in products [1].

Linde distributes its industrial gases using a network of production plants, pipeline complexes, distribution centers, and delivery vehicles [1]. Its industrial gases are distributed through one of three basic methods known as on-site or tonnage, merchant or bulk, and packaged or cylinder gases [2]. For on-site distribution, Linde constructs plants on or adjacent to the customer's site and supplies product directly to customers by pipeline [3]. Merchant deliveries are generally made from Linde's plants by tanker trucks to storage containers located at the customer's site [4]. Packaged gases are supplied in metal containers called cylinders that may be delivered directly to the customer's site or picked up by the customer at a packaging facility or retail store [5][4].
